data.command: Explain T1566.002 spear phishing via link

data.text:
Spear phishing via link, also known as T1566.002, is a type of attack where a malicious actor sends a targeted email with a link that appears to be from a trusted source, but actually leads to a malicious website or downloads malware. This type of attack is highly effective because it takes advantage of the victim's trust in the sender.

In this attack, the actor might use a technique called "typosquatting" to create a link that looks similar to the legitimate one, but with a small variation in the URL. For example, if the legitimate link is https://example.com/payments, the attacker might send a link that looks like https://example.com/paayments (note the extra "y").

The attacker might also use a technique called "URL obfuscation" to hide the true destination of the link. This can be done by using a URL shortener, a redirect service, or a script that generates a seemingly random URL.

When the victim clicks on the link, they might be redirected to a malicious website that tries to exploit a vulnerability in their browser, or download a malicious file that installs malware on their system.
